texts.facts: 5 the petitioners seek consequential relief of quashing of R.C.C. No. 10/2005 registered against them for the offences punishable under Section 7 (i) read with Sections 2 (ia) (a) and 2 (ia) (m) punishable under Sections 16 (1) (a) (i), 16 (1) (a) (ii) and 17 (1) (a) (i) and 17 (1) (b) of the Act of 1954 and the Rules of 1955. 3] Learned ASGI and learned advocate appearing for the Food Safety and Standard Authority of India opposed the petitions on the ground that after enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and repeal of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954, as per Section 97 of the Act of 2006, the challenge in the petitions to Protocol A.18.04 has become infructuous. 4] On merits, it is submitted that edible grains upto 2% by weight are permitted in Dal Chana as the same can be removed by the consumers before its use / consumption, however, in case of "Besan", it being in powder form, such foreign ingredients are not permitted as it is not possible for the consumers to remove the same. It is submitted that the protocols are Judgment 7 wp31.09+.odt prepared on recommendation of experts, keeping in view the issues relating to the health of the consumers.
texts.arguments: In these petitions, the challenge is to the validity of Protocol A.18.04 of Appendix B of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short "the Rules of 1955") which lays down that "Besan", a product obtained by grinding the dehusked Bengal gram shall not contain any other foreign ingredient or added colouring matter. The challenge is mainly to the restriction that "Besan" shall not contain any other foreign ingredient. 2] According to the petitioners, Protocol A.18.06.12 permits upto 2% by weight other edible grains in chana dal, and if other edible grains upto 2% are found in Chana Dal, it is not treated as an "adulterated" article of food as defined by Section 2 (ia) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short "the Act of 1954"). The petitioners contend that Protocol A.18.04 of Appendix B of the Rules of 1955, laying down that any other Judgment 6 wp31.09+.odt foreign ingredient is not permissible in "Besan" is arbitrary and illegal inasmuch as if edible grains upto 2% by weight are permitted in Dal Chana, then to same extent, it should be permitted in "Besan" also as "Besan" is nothing but pulverized form of Dal Chana.
texts.petitioner_arguments: In these petitions, the challenge is to the validity of Protocol A.18.04 of Appendix B of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short "the Rules of 1955") which lays down that "Besan", a product obtained by grinding the dehusked Bengal gram shall not contain any other foreign ingredient or added colouring matter. The challenge is mainly to the restriction that "Besan" shall not contain any other foreign ingredient. 2] According to the petitioners, Protocol A.18.06.12 permits upto 2% by weight other edible grains in chana dal, and if other edible grains upto 2% are found in Chana Dal, it is not treated as an "adulterated" article of food as defined by Section 2 (ia) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short "the Act of 1954"). The petitioners contend that Protocol A.18.04 of Appendix B of the Rules of 1955, laying down that any other Judgment 6 wp31.09+.odt foreign ingredient is not permissible in "Besan" is arbitrary and illegal inasmuch as if edible grains upto 2% by weight are permitted in Dal Chana, then to same extent, it should be permitted in "Besan" also as "Besan" is nothing but pulverized form of Dal Chana.
